reviews.title: Works great for my 3 monitor set up.
reviews.comment: My  NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060  was giving me trouble with annoying horizontal lines across the bottom of the screen, And it wasn't that old . After spending hours troubleshooting, I gave up and tried this card. I have 3 QHD monitors running in  2560 x 1440 mode. I don't do gaming - I work with huge photographic files. Since I put this inexpensive card in everything has been running smoothly.
reviews.author: Art Thompson

reviews.title: Not compatible with window 11
reviews.comment:
I purchased this video card using a windows 10 desk top wanting to use 3 monitors, my desk top only had the VGA and DI display ports on my desk top. My monitors uses HDMI. When I connected the monitors they all started to flicker when starting the computer and rebooting. I then had to upgrade to a window 11 computer and in installed the video card in the Dell computer. On boot up the monitors went pink and looked like a shattered window with all different colors. I tried to reload drivers everything but could not get it to work and found out that 1 of the 4 HDMI ports was not recognized and that to was causing the pink and shattered looks.
I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS VIDEO CARD TO ANYONE WHO HAS WINDOS 11.  I would have returned it within the first week if I would have known it was not working properly. Thanks AMD - Radeon RX 560 for not checking for properly working.

reviews.title: Additional Monitor Internal Connections
reviews.comment: Easy to insert. Truly plug and play. Gave me the hub to install and operate additional monitors. I am using three, although there are four jacks. I do not know if your computer will support three or four monitors. Mine will support three, but probably too taxing for the system to support four.
reviews.author: Cjbat

reviews.title: needed extra monitors and this helped
reviews.comment:
This Xynsviu Radeon RX560 2G graphics card is a pretty good pick if you need to run a bunch of screens. It's got four HDMI ports, which is real handy for folks like me who need more desk space for things like stock tracking. Keeps everything steady and gives you a much wider view so you're not always flicking between interfaces.
Getting it up and running was pretty easy, just install the drivers and your monitors should turn on. It's a low power card, so it just uses the power from the PCI Express slot, no extra cables needed. The fan is quiet and does a good job keeping it cool. It's a solid choice if you're not planning on heavy gaming but want a trustworthy card for everyday office stuff, watching videos, or even some light games. Works with Windows 7, 10, and 11, so it's good for most systems.
